title: Contextual Policy Editor: permission journeys and membership preview
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design a contextual policy editing surface for RBAC v2 that lets admins edit role permissions and assign members with immediate visibility into effective access, audit trail implications, and SSO/SAML mappings. The surface should support both compact quick edits and a detailed simulation mode for safety-sensitive changes.
background: Current console role management UX splits 'roles' and 'members' into separate flows. With RBAC v2 we need an editor that reduces mental overhead for admins, prevents accidental privilege escalation, and surfaces audit logging and SAML mapping consequences inline. This ticket scopes the primary UX for the editor and the membership assignment flow with simulated impact and preview tooling.
goals: Provide an inline preview of effective permissions when editing a role
Enable quick member assignment with suggested roles based on activity patterns and past assignments
Surface audit-log and SSO mapping consequences before commit
Allow safe experimentation: an isolated simulation mode with example API/console actions
Support compact (summary) and expanded (detailed) editor modes for different admin personas
user_stories: As an org admin, I want to add a team member to a role and immediately see which projects and routes they'll be able to access so I can avoid granting too-broad permissions.
As a security reviewer, I want to run a simulated 'what-if' to see audit log entries and SAML attribute mappings for proposed changes before approving them.
As an operations lead, I want the editor to suggest a default role based on the member's recent activity and common assignments to speed onboarding.
As a power user, I want keyboard-first flows for bulk member assignment and a compact table to review differences across role variants.
As a compliance officer, I want a clear link to the audit log for every permission change and a snapshot export for review.
decisions: Use a single combined editor panel that contains permission groups, assignment panel, and simulation canvas to reduce context switching
Provide two editor modes: Summary (compact) and Explore (detailed with simulation). Default to Summary for org-admins and to Explore when an action touches high-risk permissions
Show SAML attribute mapping hints inline when a role contains SSO-related permissions
Introduce an explicit "Preview audit entries" CTA that renders a concise audit log diff before commit
Require a secondary confirmation for changes that add any permission labeled 'high' or 'admin'
tradeoffs: Single-panel approach reduces navigation but makes the editor denser — mitigated with collapsible groups and keyboard shortcuts
Inline SAML hints add cognitive load to the editor; we hide advanced mapping details behind a tooltip and link to SSO mapping documentation

Simulation mode increases engineering surface area (backend staging execution); initial launch will use a lightweight client-side simulation for common actions and server-side dry-run for critical permissions
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows combined editor with permission groups, membership suggester, and audit preview in both Summary and Explore modes
Member suggestion algorithm surfaces at least one helpful role suggestion for >65% of test accounts in research sessions
Simulation canvas demonstrates 3 example console actions and a mock audit diff for each proposed change
Safety flow triggers secondary confirmation when modifying any permission with label 'high'
Design handoff includes component specs, interaction states, and keyboard shortcuts for bulk assignment
